video_title: Why the Next AI Breakthrough May Come from Physics
gist: Max Welling (co-founder/CTO of KUSP AI, University of Amsterdam professor) argues physics concepts -- equivariance, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and wave/symmetry-breaking dynamics -- are not just applications for AI but literal design principles for next-generation architectures, while detailing KUSP AI's generative-AI materials-discovery platform (carbon capture, semiconductors, perovskites, batteries) which is roughly two years and $30M into building toward its first AI-discovered material in a shipping device.

themes.theme: KUSP AI — Funding, Team & Business Model

insights.claim: KUSP AI was founded in spring 2024 by Max Welling and Chad Edwards with an initial raise of about $30 million, and has grown to roughly 50 people across labs in Amsterdam, Cambridge (HQ), London and Berlin, with expansion underway into Asia and North America.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: A ~2-year-old, $30M-seeded, ~50-person startup with multi-continent lab footprint and active expansion signals it is scaling for a broader fundraise or partnership push soon.
insights.quote: we started with a good initial investment of about 30 million uh from which we could hire an excellent team

insights.claim: KUSP AI's advisory board pairs AI godfathers Jeff Hinton and Yan Lun (Yann LeCun) with deep industrial/regulatory figures: Martin Vandenbrink, former President and CTO of ASML, and Lord Brown, former CEO of BP, plus Varity Harding (UK government/DeepMind) and Kristin Persson (founder of the Materials Project database).
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: The advisor mix (AI research heavyweights plus semiconductor and energy-industry veterans) signals KUSP is positioning specifically for semiconductor-materials and energy-transition partnerships/customers, not pure academic prestige.

insights.claim: KUSP AI runs a dual business model: a partnership track where it works with academic labs and corporate R&D teams to design and synthesize materials for their specific needs, and a self-funded internal-project track where KUSP retains full IP on discoveries and then seeks customers to license it to.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: The IP-retention track means KUSP can capture more value from any breakthrough material than a pure fee-for-service model would, but it also means KUSP is carrying discovery risk on its own balance sheet.

insights.claim: KUSP AI has an active but undisclosed contract with a large national lab in Asia for scaled experimental materials work, plus a live perovskite-solar-cell lab engagement in Amsterdam and a catalysis project with DTU (Danish Technical University), indicating real institutional customer traction beyond the concept stage.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: Multiple concurrent, named institutional lab engagements (even if commercial terms are undisclosed) are a concrete pipeline signal for a company still short of a flagship commercialized material.

insights.claim: KUSP AI (with Nvidia) recently open-sourced 'CUPS,' a universal particle/molecular-dynamics simulator that compiles machine-learning force fields into JAX so they run efficiently and in parallel on GPUs, released roughly a week before this interview at ICLR to a strong reception.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: Open-sourcing core simulation infrastructure with Nvidia is a classic ecosystem/adoption play that could make KUSP's force-field approach a default tooling layer for the AI-for-science community, ahead of monetizing the discovery platform itself.
insights.quote: we released this open source a few days ago actually or a week ago at iClar

insights.claim: KUSP AI's competitive moat includes exclusive literature-licensing deals with major scientific publishing houses, whose content is ingested into a proprietary materials database that its search agent queries before generating any novel candidate molecules.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: Exclusive data licensing is a defensible, hard-to-replicate input advantage distinct from model architecture -- worth tracking as a moat comparable to proprietary datasets in other AI verticals.

insights.claim: KUSP AI's generative platform now spans well beyond its original carbon-capture metal-organic-framework (MOF) work into semiconductors, perovskite solar-cell materials, battery materials, fuel cells and PFAS-removal materials from water, making it a horizontal advanced-materials platform rather than a single-application company.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: A platform strategy across multiple large material end-markets (energy, chips, water treatment) diversifies KUSP's commercial optionality but also dilutes near-term focus versus a single flagship product.

insights.claim: Neural-network surrogate 'force fields' that replace expensive quantum-mechanical (DFT/Schrodinger-equation) force calculations deliver roughly three to four orders of magnitude speedup versus the quantum approximations, and this efficiency gain is the core economic unlock that makes large-scale generative material search computationally feasible.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: A 1,000-10,000x compute-cost reduction versus classical quantum chemistry is the specific mechanism justifying AI-for-materials valuations -- an investor can sanity-check discovery-platform claims against this benchmark.
insights.quote: three orders or four order magnitude acceleration more efficiency relative to these quantum mechanical approximations

insights.claim: KUSP AI's end-to-end discovery pipeline runs: query an ingested literature/patent database for existing near-matches; if none exist, a generative model proposes hundreds of thousands of candidate molecules against specified property constraints; cheap computational filters (ground-state relaxation, charge/stability checks, pore size) prune the pool; distilled machine-learning force fields run molecular-dynamics simulation to estimate properties; results feed a higher-scale PDE/device model; and only on the order of ten or fewer surviving candidates ever reach a physical lab experiment.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: This funnel (hundreds of thousands -> ~10 physical candidates) is the template investors should expect other AI-for-science platforms to replicate; the defensibility lives in the filtering/distillation steps, not just the generative model.

insights.claim: KUSP AI's chemistry foundation models are trained on large DFT datasets -- the Materials Project database and a dataset built with Meta -- and then distilled/fine-tuned into smaller, fast, material-class-specific models, which is necessary because molecular-dynamics simulation calls the force-field model at femtosecond-scale steps many millions of times per simulation.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: The Materials Project/Meta-data dependency and the distillation step are both potential single points of external reliance -- worth watching whether KUSP builds proprietary training data over time to reduce that dependency.

insights.claim: Molecules can be represented either as 3D-equivariant graph neural networks or as 1D SMILES-string sequences processed LLM-style, and KUSP can even fuse scientific-literature text tokens with molecular-graph tokens in a single model, effectively merging chemistry foundation models with LLM architectures.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: The convergence of LLM-style tokenization with molecular graph representations suggests AI-for-science platforms will increasingly ride the same scaling and tooling improvements as mainstream LLM infrastructure, not a separate technical stack.

insights.claim: Some of KUSP's scientists report being able to do in a few days what previously took a PhD researcher much longer, but Welling is explicit this is a qualitative, simulation/digital-domain-only observation, not a validated quantitative hit-rate comparison against traditional experimental discovery.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: Investors should discount productivity claims from AI-for-science startups that are anecdotal and simulation-only until backed by controlled hit-rate data against the pre-AI baseline.
insights.quote: what we can do now in a few days what took a PhD before

insights.claim: Even after reaching net-zero emissions, Welling estimates roughly 50 to 100 more years will be needed of continued atmospheric carbon removal at about 20 gigatons of CO2 per year -- a volume he likens to filling Lake Geneva with liquid CO2 -- with energy cost and sorbent-material cost as the two largest cost drivers of that removal.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: This frames direct-air-capture materials as a multi-decade, massive-volume market where sorbent-material cost (KUSP's target) is one of only two dominant cost levers -- a specific angle for sizing the carbon-capture materials TAM.

insights.claim: The metal-organic-framework (MOF) material class that was the subject of KUSP's first internally self-funded project -- carbon-capture sorbents -- is the same material class that won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry this year (credited by Welling to Kitagawa, Yaghi and Robson), validating KUSP's early strategic bet on that material family.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: External Nobel-level validation of a material class a startup bet on early is a credibility signal that can support future fundraising and partnership narratives, independent of KUSP's own results.
insights.quote: this is the material that this year won the Nobel Prize in chemistry

insights.claim: Roughly 100,000 MOF molecules have historically been synthesized and structurally verified by chemists in labs -- the existing human-generated baseline that KUSP's generative search is designed to expand well beyond by designing task-specific novel molecules from scratch.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: A concrete existing-catalog size (~100K) gives a benchmark against which to judge how many genuinely novel, KUSP-discovered molecules eventually reach production -- a trackable KPI for the platform's real output.
insights.quote: actually made maybe around 100,000 of these molecules in labs

insights.claim: 'Self-driving labs' (automated robotic experimentation) are described as the current revolution in materials science, enabling on the order of 100 experiments per day versus much slower manual lab work, and KUSP is actively integrating its discovery platform with this automated-experiment loop.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: The pairing of generative candidate-proposal with automated high-throughput physical testing is the mechanism that could compress materials-discovery timelines from years to months industry-wide; watch which platforms achieve tight closed-loop integration first.
insights.quote: you can do maybe a 100 experiments a day

insights.claim: Despite roughly two years of operation and a $30M+ raise, KUSP AI has not yet reached its own stated proof-point milestone: a material that could not have been designed without AI, successfully integrated into an actual shipping device (e.g., a semiconductor chip or solar cell) for a paying customer -- Welling frames this as still forthcoming.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: This is an explicit expectations-setter from the company's own CTO: the flagship commercial proof point for AI-designed materials is still ahead, not behind -- a useful gut-check against more bullish AI-for-science narratives.
insights.quote: I'm really looking forward to to discovering a material that is unique

insights.claim: Welling's forthcoming book argues that the mathematics of modern generative AI (diffusion models, variational autoencoders, MCMC sampling, free-energy estimation) is not merely analogous to but mathematically equivalent to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics/thermodynamics, because both fields are fundamentally built on information theory describing the loss of information over time.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: If the equivalence is literal rather than metaphorical, tools and theorems from a century of physics can be directly ported into generative-model design and analysis, implying a large untapped toolkit for the next wave of architecture innovation.
insights.quote: at the core of physics is information theory and in the core of machine learning is information theory

insights.claim: Landauer's principle -- that erasing one bit of information from a device forces the release of a fixed quantity of energy as heat -- is cited by Welling as direct physical evidence linking Shannon information to conservation laws, reinforcing the claim that entropy in thermodynamics and entropy in machine learning describe the same underlying phenomenon.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: This is the specific physical law Welling leans on to argue the ML/thermodynamics link is literal, not poetic -- useful for evaluating how rigorous the book's central claim actually is.

insights.claim: The original 2015 paper that introduced diffusion models explicitly used the term 'non-equilibrium thermodynamics' in its title, meaning the physics-generative-AI connection was recognized at the method's inception rather than being a retrospective reinterpretation by Welling.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: This dates the physics/generative-AI link back to diffusion models' origin, meaning the connection Welling's book formalizes is timing-consistent with the whole diffusion-model wave, not a new post-hoc framing.
insights.quote: the first paper that was written about diffusion models actually had the word non-equilibrium thermodynamics in the title

insights.claim: Modern diffusion-model methods can be used to accelerate a core pharma/biotech computation -- estimating the free-energy difference between an unbound protein and a drug candidate versus the bound (drug-attached) state -- giving chemists a faster route to predicting binding affinity.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: This is a concrete, named application of generative-AI-for-physics techniques directly relevant to drug-discovery economics, distinct from KUSP's own materials-science focus -- a candidate area to watch for AI-biotech tooling plays.

insights.claim: In the reverse direction, 'counterdiabatic driving,' a control technique developed in stochastic thermodynamics for efficiently steering physical systems, is being imported into diffusion models to reduce statistical noise/error during the generative sampling process, improving image and video model quality.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: A specific, named physics-control technique already improving mainstream image/video diffusion models is a concrete example of physics-derived methods quietly entering production generative-AI systems.

insights.claim: Stochastic (non-equilibrium) thermodynamics is itself a young, still-actively-researched field, and Welling argues it offers a genuinely new vocabulary -- heat, work, entropy production -- for interpreting the internal mechanics of foundation models, which he says the AI field currently understands only at a surface level.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: If physics vocabulary becomes a genuine interpretability lens for foundation models, it could open a differentiated research/product niche (physics-informed interpretability tools) distinct from mainstream mechanistic-interpretability approaches.

themes.theme: Physics-AI Convergence — Waves & Symmetry Breaking in Neural Architecture

insights.claim: Newer multi-electrode brain recordings (hundreds to thousands of simultaneous electrodes versus single-electrode measurements previously) have revealed traveling waves throughout the brain that earlier single-point measurement technology could not detect, leaving open whether these waves are functionally important to cognition or merely a side effect.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: This is a live open question in neuroscience that is directly motivating new neural-network architecture research -- worth tracking as a leading indicator for where brain-inspired AI research may head next.
insights.quote: people have now observed them everywhere

insights.claim: 'Over-smoothing' -- where a signal introduced at a deep neural network's input is exponentially suppressed across thousands of layers until the input and output become statistically independent -- is identified as a core unsolved problem in deep learning that motivates borrowing wave physics as a fix.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: Naming over-smoothing as the specific failure mode gives investors and researchers a concrete technical target: any architecture claiming to solve long-range information flow should be benchmarked against this problem.
insights.quote: the input and the output of the neural network become independent of each other

insights.claim: Welling's team has built neural networks that generate internal traveling waves via dedicated 'memory channels' or 'capsules' to move and preserve information over long depth or time, drawing the analogy to how phonons carry vibrational information through materials and how light waves let telescopes see across the universe.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: This is a distinct, physics-grounded alternative to attention/state-space mechanisms for long-range information transport in neural networks -- a research direction worth tracking alongside transformers and SSMs.

insights.claim: Welling reports his wave-based neural networks outperform standard RNNs on long-horizon memory tasks, such as holding two numbers introduced at long, random time gaps in a sequence and correctly summing them on demand.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: A concrete task-level win over RNNs on long-range memory is an early empirical result, though no exact numbers were given -- worth watching for a published benchmark against transformers/state-space models too.

insights.claim: Welling frames 'edge of chaos' as the governing dynamical-systems principle: both brains and the best-performing neural networks operate in a narrow regime between a stable phase (inputs collapse to a single point, losing information -- analogous to vanishing gradients) and a chaotic phase (information is technically preserved but numerically untrackable -- analogous to exploding gradients and rising entropy), and his wave-based architectures naturally sit at this edge without manual tuning.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: 'Edge of chaos' gives a portable diagnostic for evaluating any new architecture's stability/expressivity trade-off, and an architecture that lands there automatically avoids a hyperparameter-tuning burden that competing designs still carry.
insights.quote: neural networks that perform best operate at this edge of chaos

insights.claim: The specific mechanism Welling uses to generate beneficial traveling waves is spontaneous symmetry breaking: baking a large artificial symmetry into extra per-neuron dimensions, then using sufficiently large-variance random weights to spontaneously break that symmetry, which produces near-zero-energy oscillating (Goldstone-mode-like) waves that propagate the full depth of the network -- directly importing the condensed-matter mechanism behind phenomena like water freezing into ice as a neural-architecture design principle.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: This is a genuinely novel, patentable-style architectural design principle (symmetry-breaking-induced waves) rather than an incremental tweak -- a distinctive technical thread to track if KUSP or Welling's academic group publishes benchmark results at scale.
insights.quote: we use something a deep result from physics as a design principle for neural networks

insights.claim: Welling signals this is an open-ended research program, stating there are many more physics concepts still to be mined for AI architecture design, positioning equivariance, thermodynamics, and wave/symmetry-breaking dynamics as a recurring, generalizable toolkit rather than a one-off trick.
insights.speaker: Max Welling
insights.so_what: If physics-derived priors keep yielding new architecture classes, groups with deep physics expertise (like Welling's) may have a durable, hard-to-replicate research edge over pure scaling-focused labs.
